form.context: Aurora Storefront login page. Shoppers sign in with an email address and a password.
form.user_story: As a shopper, I want my Aurora Storefront account to lock quickly after too many wrong passwords so that my account stays safe.

generated_acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Shopper account locks after repeated wrong passwords
  Given a registered shopper with an active Aurora Storefront account
  When they submit a wrong password 5 times in a row
  Then the account locks within 60 seconds of the fifth attempt
  And they see 'Account locked. Try again in 15 minutes.'

Scenario: Successful login before the lockout threshold
  Given a registered shopper with an active Aurora Storefront account
  When they submit the correct password on the third attempt
  Then they are signed in and redirected to the shop homepage
  And the failed-attempt counter resets to zero

Scenario: Locked account rejects even the correct password
  Given a shopper account locked after 5 failed attempts
  When they submit the correct password during the lockout window
  Then they stay signed out
  And they see 'Account locked. Try again in 15 minutes.'

Scenario: Lockout expires and shopper can try again
  Given a shopper account locked after 5 failed attempts
  When 15 minutes pass since the lock
  Then the next correct password signs them in

Scenario: Shopper is notified about the lockout by email
  Given a shopper account that has just been locked
  When the lock is applied
  Then Aurora Storefront sends a lockout notification email within 1 minute

Scenario: Locked account cannot be brute-forced during the window
  Given a shopper account locked after 5 failed attempts
  When 100 further password guesses arrive within the lockout window
  Then all of them are rejected without checking the password hash
result.invest_estimable: FAIL -- 'quickly' and 'too many' have no measurable boundaries, so no estimate is possible
result.invest_independent: PARTIAL -- lockout depends on the existing sign-in flow and email service
result.invest_overall: PARTIAL -- boundaries and testability are missing, but the goal is clear
result.invest_small: PARTIAL -- lock plus notification plus expiry may exceed one short story
result.invest_testable: FAIL -- 'quickly', 'too many' and 'stays safe' cannot be verified as written
result.invest_valuable: PARTIAL -- account safety matters, but no quantified value or affected segment
missing_elements: No error handling specified (locked-account login attempts, email failure)
No data boundaries (attempt count, lockout duration, reset window)
No NFRs (lock timing target, brute-force rate limit)
No pre-conditions (account exists and is active)
No post-conditions (counter reset, audit entry written)
recommended_split: Lock the account after 5 failed password attempts within 10 minutes
Notify the shopper by email when a lockout happens
Unlock automatically after 15 minutes and reset the counter
risks: Developers will each pick their own lockout threshold, causing inconsistent protection across environments
Without a notification scenario, takeovers may go unnoticed by shoppers
Without a defined lockout window, support cannot answer 'when can I sign in again'
Missing rate limiting invites brute-force attacks during the lockout window

suggested_rewrites: Replace 'quickly' with a measurable target: 'within 60 seconds of the fifth failed attempt'
Replace 'too many' with a number: '5 failed password attempts within 10 minutes'
Replace 'stays safe' with the observable outcome: 'no further password guesses are checked until the lockout expires'
Name the actor precisely: 'a registered shopper with an active account'
